title: Edit a plan's rules table in a throwaway editor

parts.text: Turn one awkward section of an HTML plan into a temporary editing app, then export the revised rules back into the plan.
Identify an editing challenge: choose one structured section that is painful to edit in raw HTML, such as a table of visualization rules.
Prompt for a custom editing UI: ask for a small, disposable, self-contained HTML editor with an export in the same format as the source section.
Use the throwaway micro-app: change the rules through its controls, and test adding, deleting and reordering an item.
Integrate the refined output: copy the export, validate its structure, paste it into the plan and reopen the plan.
Every source rule appears in the editor without losing values.
You can add, remove, and change entries without editing HTML by hand.
The exported data matches the format expected by the main plan.
The editor changes or drops fields from the source data: give a representative input and the exact output schema.
Edits disappear when the page reloads: add import and export controls plus local browser storage.
Claude builds a full application instead of a focused editor: restate the single editing job.
The export cannot be pasted back into the plan: add a validator that shows errors next to the field.
